newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-JUVENTUS START WITH ONLY FIVE SURVIVORS FROM '96 FINAL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-JUVENTUS START WITH ONLY FIVE SURVIVORS FROM '96 FINAL.

text.p: Juventus manager Marcello Lippi named just five players who appeared in last year's European Cup final in the team attempting to retain the trophy against Borussia Dortmund at the Olympic Stadium on Wednesday.

The only survivors from the winning side 12 months ago were goalkeeper Angelo Peruzzi, defender Ciro Ferrara and midfielder Didier Deschamps along with Angelo Di Livio and Vladimir Jugovic who both came on as substitutes in last year's final.

Paulo Sousa, who played in last year's Juventus team, was in the Dortmund lineup against his former club. Three other Dortmund players -- Stefan Reuter, Andreas Moeller and Juergen Kohler are also former Juve players.

Dortmund manager Ottmar Hitzfeld, who has used 24 players during his team's route to their first European Cup final, left out Rene Tretschok and Lars Ricken, the players whose goals secured a 2-0 aggregate win over Manchester United in the semifinals, from the starting lineup.
European Player of the Year Matthias Sammer returned as libero with Portugese midfielder Paulo Sousa returning in midfield.

The Olympic Stadium was bathed in evening sunlight at the kickoff of a match being watched in a record number of 202 countries and territories around the world with an estimated global audience of 500 million.

But then against the run of play Dortmund took the lead with their first shot of the match after 29 minutes. Juventus goalkeeper Peruuzi failed to get hold of Moeller's corner punching the ball only as far as Paul Lambert on the righthand side of the Juve penalty area.
Lambert swung over a high ball which beat the Italian defence and came to Karlheinz Reidle who chested it down before lashing it left-footed past Peruzzi.
Five minutes later Dortmund were astonishingly 2-0 ahead with a goal of stunning simplicity. Moeller took another corner from the left and Riedle rose unmarked to head home.

The Italian players looked shell-shocked and Juve coach Marcello Lippi stood at the touchline hardly able to believe the sudden turnaround after his side had dominated the opening half- an-hour so comprehensively.
Juventus were unlucky to go into the interval without a goal to their credit.

Three minutes before halftime the Italians went desperately close to scoring when midfielder Zinedine Zidane hit the post. A minute later striker Christian Vieri put the ball into the net but was judged to have handled.
Juventus brought on forward Alessandro del Piero for defender Sergio Porrini at the start of the second half as the Italians were forced to push forward.
In the 54th minute Vladimir Jugovic went close with a low, long-range shot which Dortmund goalkeeper Stefan Klos just managed to turn around his left-hand post.
Shortly afterwards Klos had to save the Germans again, pushing a shot from Vieri on to the bar.
On the hour Alen Boksic headed into the German keeper's arms as the Italians piled on the pressure.
Juventus then scored a brilliant goal in the 64th minute to get back into the match.
Boksic made a weaving run down the left-hand side and hit over a superb low cross for del Piero to flick the ball into the net from close range.
In the 67th minute Dortmund coach Ottmar Hitzfeld brought on Heiko Herrlich for Riedle who had been suffering with a shin problem before the match.
Then Dortmund youngster Lars Ricken produced a goal which will go down as one of the most remarkable moments in European Cup final history.
Just 16 seconds after coming on for Stephane Chapuisat in the 70th minute, Ricken broke free down the right flank and lobbed the ball over Peruzzi from some 20 metres out to give Dortmund a 3-1 lead.
